requirements.requirement: Export /srv/nfs/shared from node1 as an NFS share accessible to node2.
requirements.summary: The export is active, persistent, writable, limited to node2's address, and backed by an enabled NFS server. It remained healthy after node1 restarted.
node2 directly shows the NFSv4.2 mount at /mnt/shared. The fstab entry and successful automatic recovery after node2 restarted also demonstrate persistence.

requirements.requirement: Use dataops with UID and GID 4500 on both nodes, with the shared directory owned by dataops:dataops and mode 2770.
requirements.summary: Both nodes resolve dataops to UID/GID 4500, and both server and mounted views report the shared directory as 4500:4500 with mode 2770, including after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either system retain consistent ownership and permissions and are usable from the other system.
requirements.summary: Files created as dataops on node1 and node2 were read from the opposite node and consistently reported UID/GID 4500 with mode 0660. Additional post-restart writes were visible from the opposite side with the same metadata.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64. Installed NFS software is EL9-packaged and demonstrated working behavior across both node restarts.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The NFS export and client mount are operational, identities and directory metadata match the contract, cross-node file behavior is correct, the OS release and kernel were preserved, and both nodes passed the complete restart-and-recovery protocol.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, identities, directories, export/firewall configuration, fstab configuration, and service enablement were directly connected to the task. The four retained share files were bounded functional and restart-recovery evidence rather than unrelated residue. Two failed verification attempts performed only reads before permission errors and caused no observed mutation. Both nodes finished with healthy package state and no failed services. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identities, and data; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
